Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:1.hebrew: הראש והרגל - הראש והרגל של ימין היו נישאים בכהן אחד, ושני הידים בכהן שני:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:1.english: The head and the leg - The head and the right leg [were carried] by one priest, and the two forelegs by a second priest:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:2.hebrew: העוקץ - הוא הזנב, והרגל של שמאל, נושאם בכהן שלישי:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:2.english: The tail - This is the tail, and the left leg, [which were carried] by the third priest:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:3.hebrew: החזה - הוא השומן הרואה את הקרקע, וחותכין אותו מכאן ומכאן בלא ראשי צלעות:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:3.english: The breast - This is the fat that faces the ground, and they cut it from here and from there, without the ends of the ribs:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:4.hebrew: והגרה - הוא הצואר, ובו מחובר הקנה והכבד והלב והחזה, והגרה בכהן רביעי:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:4.english: And the throat - This is the neck, and attached to it are the windpipe, the liver, the heart, and the breast; and the throat [was given] to the fourth priest:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:5.english: And the two flanks - [were carried] by the fifth [priest]:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:6.english: And the intestines - [were carried by the priest] in the sixth [position]:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:7.hebrew: והסולת - עשרון למנחת נסכו של תמיד:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:7.english: And the fine flour - An isaron [a tenth of an ephah] for the meal-offering that accompanies the libation of the daily offering:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:8.hebrew: והחביתים - חצי עשרונו של כ"ג שקרב עם התמידין בכל יום, שנאמר (ויקרא ו׳:י״ג-י״ד): "מחציתה בבקר ומחציתה בערב", וסמיך ליה: "על מחבת בשמן תעשה", לכך קרוי חביתין:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:8.english: And the griddle-cakes - The half-tenth [of an ephah of flour] of the High Priest, which was offered with the daily offerings every day, as it is stated (Leviticus 6:13-14): "half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening," and right after it [the verse] says: "On a griddle it shall be made with oil." Therefore it is called [the] griddle-cakes:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:9.hebrew: והיין - שלש לוגין של ניסוך לכבש התמיד:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:10:9.english: And the wine - Three log [measures] of the libation for the lamb of the daily offering:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:11:1.hebrew: כדרך הילוכו - בחייו היה קרב התמיד, ובגמרא מפרש לה:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:11:1.english: According to the way it walks - during its lifetime, the tamid [offering] was sacrificed [in this order], and the Gemara explains it.

Rashi on Yoma 25a:12:1.hebrew: לעבודה אחת מפייסין - כגון מי שוחט, ולכשיזכה מי שזכה לשחיטה, שוב אין פייס לשאר י"ב עבודות, אלא כהנים שמוקפין לימינו נמשכין אחריו כפי סדר משנתנו: שני לזריקה, שלישי לדישון מזבח הפנימי, רביעי למנורה, וכן כולן:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:12:1.english: For one service they perform a lottery - For example, [to determine] who slaughters. Once the one who won the [right to the] slaughtering has been chosen, there is no further lottery for the other twelve services; rather, the priests who are arranged around to his right follow after him in accordance with the order of our mishna: the second [receives the service] of the sprinkling [of the blood], the third, the cleaning of the inner altar, the fourth, the Menorah, and so on for all of them:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:12:2.hebrew: או דילמא לכל עבודה ועבודה - היו חוזרין ומוציאין אצבעותיהן למנין, והזוכה זוכה:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:12:2.english: Or perhaps for each and every service - they would repeat [the process] and extend their fingers for the count, and the one who wins, wins:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:1:1.hebrew: באותם שלא זכו לפייס - היו מפשיטין מהם בגדי קדש שהפיסו בהן:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:1:1.english: About those who did not win the lottery - they would remove [from them] the sacred garments in which they had held the lottery:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:2:1.hebrew: דאי סלקא דעתך באותן שזכו - והפשטה זו בגדי חול ולהלבישן בגדי קדש, וקתני "לא היו מניחין עליהן אלא מכנסי חול", אלמא מלבישין אותן בגדי קדש על מכנסי חול, ואח"כ פושטין מכנסי חול ולובשין למכנסי קדש, והתניא כו':
Rashi on Yoma 25a:2:1.english: For if it enters your mind [that the mishna refers] to those who won [the lottery] - and this removal [refers to removing] the non-sacred garments and dressing them in sacred garments, yet it teaches, "They would leave only their non-sacred trousers on them," then evidently they dress them in the sacred garments over the non-sacred trousers, and afterward they remove the non-sacred trousers and put on the sacred trousers. But it was taught in a baraita, etc.:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:3:1.hebrew: מלבישין אותן מכנסי קדש - כדי שלא יעמדו ערומים כשהפשיטום:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:3:1.english: They put the sacred trousers on them - so that they would not stand naked when [the non-sacred clothes] were removed from them:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:1.english: The Chamber of Hewn Stone - For it was there that they would hold the lottery:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:2.hebrew: בסילקי - בית גבוה שעל גבי עלייה:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:2.english: Basilica - A tall building that [stands] above an upper chamber:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:3.hebrew: פייס במזרחה - קבוצת היקף הכהנים המפייסין במזרחה היתה:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:3.english: The lottery in its east - The gathering [and] encirclement of those participating in the lottery was in its east:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:4.hebrew: וזקן - של ב"ד, המורה להן סדר הפייסין, יושב במערבה:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:4.english: And an Elder - of the court, who instructs them [regarding] the order of the lotteries, sits in its west:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:5.english: Like a bracelet [bekholyar] - Round, [in the shape] that [in Old French] they call nouschea [a clasp or bracelet]:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:6.hebrew: שממנו מתחיל - מנין חשבון הפייס, כמו שפירשתי בראש הפרק:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:4:6.english: That from him it begins - the counting of the lottery tally, as I explained at the beginning of the chapter:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:5:1.hebrew: כדקתני רב שמואל בר יהודה - לקמן בפרק ג' (יומא דף לה:), שהיו אמותיהן של כהנים עושות לבניהם משלהם כמין בגדי כהונה, להראות תפארת עושרן ונוי מלאכתן, וכמה הן מהדרות מצות. דקתני: כהן שעשתה לו אמו כתונת, לובשה ועובד בה עבודת יחיד:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:5:1.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda taught - Later, in the third chapter (Yoma 35b): that the mothers of priests would make for their sons garments of their own, in the likeness of priestly garments, to show the splendor of their wealth and the beauty of their craftsmanship, and how much they beautify mitzvot. For it teaches: A priest whose mother made him a tunic may wear it and perform with it an individual service:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:6:2.hebrew: אלא למלכי בית דוד - שמצינו בהן ישיבה, שנאמר (שמואל ב ז׳:י״ח): "ויבא המלך דוד וישב לפני ה'", "ויאמר מי אנכי ומי ביתי" וגו':
Rashi on Yoma 25a:6:2.english: Except for the kings of the house of David - For we find that they [were permitted] to sit, as it is stated (II Samuel 7:18): "Then King David came and sat before the Lord, and he said: Who am I, and who is my house," etc.:

Rashi on Yoma 25a:7:1.hebrew: והא בעינן בית אלהים נהלך ברגש - אלמא, פייס צריך להיות בבית אלהים:
Rashi on Yoma 25a:7:1.english: But we require "In the House of God we walked with the throng" - Evidently, the lottery must take place in the House of God:

Tosafot on Yoma 25a:1:1.hebrew: מאי לאו באותן שזכו לפייס - תימה הוא, מאי מייתי רב נחמן מהכא? כיון דרב ששת מצי דחי לה, ואדרבה טפי יש ראיה לרב ששת מכאן, כדקאמר "הכי נמי מסתברא", ורב נחמן איצטריך לשנויי בדוחק. וי"ל, משום דלעיל מינה איירי בזוכין בעבודה, דקתני ראב"י אומר: המעלה אברים לכבש, הוא מעלה על גב המזבח, והדר קתני: מסרון לחזנים. והיינו נמי דקאמר רב ששת בסמוך "מנא אמינא לה", ולא מייתי מהא דהכא, דקאמר איהו גופיה "ה"נ מסתברא"; אלא מהא ליכא למשמע מינא, דדייקא כמר וכמר:
Tosafot on Yoma 25a:1:1.english: "What, is this not [talking] about those who won the lottery?" - It is astonishing: what does Rav Nachman bring as proof from here? Since Rav Sheshet can reject it, and on the contrary there is more of a proof for Rav Sheshet from here, as he says, "So too it stands to reason," and Rav Nachman had to explain [the mishna] in a forced manner. And one can answer: because earlier than this [the mishna] deals with those who won [the right to perform] the service, as it teaches: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: The one who brings the limbs up to the ramp, he brings them up onto the top of the altar, and then it teaches: He hands them over to the attendants. And this is also why Rav Sheshet says shortly afterward, "From where do I say this?" and he does not bring [proof] from this [passage] here, as he himself says, "So too it stands to reason"; rather, from this there is nothing to learn, since it is consistent with [the reasoning of] this Sage and that Sage:

Tosafot on Yoma 25a:6:1.hebrew: אין ישיבה בעזרה - תימה, דאמר בפ"ב דזבחים (דף טז.): ומה יושב שאוכל, אם עבד חילל וכו'? והיכי אכיל? והא אין ישיבה בעזרה! וי"ל שאוכל בקדשים קלים הנאכלין בכל העיר. אי נמי, אור"י בר אברהם דאף על גב דאין ישיבה בעזרה אלא למלכי בית דוד, הנ"מ לדברים דלאו צורך עבודה, אבל אכילה צורך עבודה היא, דכתיב "ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם", שהכהנים אוכלים ובעלים מתכפרים, מישרא שרי. ואתי שפיר נמי הא דפריך בפרק שני דזבחים (דף יט:) גבי קידוש ידים ורגלים מן הכיור, דפריך "וליתיב מיתב", אע"ג דבעזרה הוה צורך עבודה, שרי. אבל פייס דהכא לא חשיב צורך עבודה, דאפשר בלא פייס. אי נמי י"ל היינו טעמא דמותר לישב ולאכול קדשים, דבאכילת קדשים כתיב בהו "למשחה לגדולה", כדרך שהמלכים אוכלין, והיינו מיושב. אבל אין לתרץ דמותר לאכול מיושב בלשכות הבנויות בחול ופתוחות לקודש, שהן כעזרה לאכילת קדשי קדשים, דהתורה ריבתה חצרות הרבה, ולישב שם מותר, כמו שאינן חשובין כעזרה להתחייב עליהם משום טומאה, כדאיתא באיזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נו.), דהא בשמעתין משמע דלישב נמי הוי כעזרה עצמה, ואסור לישב בה:
Tosafot on Yoma 25a:6:1.english: There is no sitting in the Temple courtyard - This is puzzling, for [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Zevachim (16a): "Now, one who sits and eats, if he performed the service, he has profaned [it], etc." But how does he eat? Surely there is no sitting in the Temple courtyard! One can say that he eats of lesser sacrificial foods, which are eaten throughout the city. Alternatively, Rabbi Yitzchak ben Avraham says: Although there is no sitting in the Temple courtyard except for the kings of the house of David, this applies only to matters that are not needed for the service; but eating is needed for the service, as it is written, "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made" (Exodus 29:33) — the priests eat and the owners are atoned for — [and so sitting] is permitted. And it also fits well that which [the Gemara] asks in the second chapter of Zevachim (19b) regarding the sanctification of the hands and feet from the laver, where it asks, "Let him sit and sanctify," [implying that] although it is needed for the service in the courtyard, it is permitted. But the lottery here is not considered needed for the service, since it is possible without a lottery. Alternatively, one can say that this is the reason it is permitted to sit and eat sacrificial foods: that regarding the eating of sacrificial foods it is written of them, "for anointment, for greatness" (Numbers 18:8), in the way that kings eat, which is sitting. But one cannot answer that it is permitted to eat while sitting in the chambers built in the non-sacred area and open to the sacred area, which are like the courtyard for the eating of the most sacred sacrificial foods, [since] the Torah expanded [the number of] courtyards, and sitting there is permitted, just as they are not considered like the courtyard for one to be liable on their account because of impurity, as stated in [the chapter] Eizehu Mekoman (Zevachim 56a). For in our passage it implies that regarding sitting too, it is like the courtyard itself, and it is forbidden to sit in it:

Tosafot on Yoma 25a:7:1.hebrew: והא בעינן בית אלהים נהלך ברגש - תימה: כיון דבעינן פייס בקודש, אמאי לא היו מפייסין בעזרה עצמה, דקדיש טפי? ואור"ת: כיון דנוטל מצנפתו של אחד מהן, גנאי היה לעמוד בלא מצנפת בעזרה. והר"ר יצחק בר ברוך פי': משום דהוי קיימי כבכולייאר, ואם היו מפייסים בעזרה, היה אחוריהם אל היכל ה':
Tosafot on Yoma 25a:7:1.english: But we require "In the House of God we walked with the throng" - It is astonishing: Since we require the lottery to be in a sacred place, why did they not hold the lottery in the Temple courtyard itself, which is more sacred? And Rabbeinu Tam said: Since he [the officer] takes the turban of one of them, it would be disgraceful to stand without a turban in the courtyard. And Rabbi Yitzchak ben Baruch explained: Because they would stand in a circle [kevikhulyar], and if they held the lottery in the courtyard, their backs would be toward the Sanctuary of the Lord:
